semantic_judge.reason: The customer_insights controller applies status-based business rules (cancelled orders excluded from lifetime value and from the 'no orders' definition) rather than only decoding requests, calling services and mapping responses. Totals are delegated to summarize(), but the inclusion policy is decided in the controller. The reports controller applies the same kind of cancelled-order exclusion. The other controllers (catalog, customers, http, orders) only validate input, call services, catch exceptions and map results, so they pass.

findings.explanation: The controller decides which orders count toward a customer's lifetime value by excluding orders with status "cancelled", then sums their totals. That is a business definition of the metric, and it belongs in the application layer, not the controller.

The controller defines what counts as a customer "without orders" by treating cancelled orders as absent. This eligibility policy should be expressed by an application service, not hard-coded in the controller.
The controller decides which orders count toward units-per-SKU by excluding cancelled orders. This is a business rule about what counts as ordered demand and should live in the application layer.
